text:
alex: noticing p99 latency jump on hosted API /v2 since ~03:45 UTC. Multiple customer escalations (high throughput customers) reporting timeouts and UI freezes. p95 up ~2x, p99 up ~4x. Anyone else seeing this?
maya: seen some alerts. Datadog shows tail latency spike starting 03:42 UTC. No obvious deploys in changelog for that window.
chris: pulling traces now. Traces show a lot of requests stuck in model runtime waiting on kernel queues. High GPU queue depth on pool-us-east-1-g4.
olivia: can you paste a sample trace id? I’ll check routing and traffic splits.
chris: trace id trace_20260312_1a2b3c -> spans: frontend -> routing -> runtime-kernel -> kv-cache -> model. Longest spans are runtime-kernel 1200-1500ms.
alex: queuing looks like a spike in sequence lengths? But customer says average prompt length didn't change.
maya: support ticket 4287 says sudden p99 increases correlate with batch of longer system prompts from one customer (auto-summarize job). Could be bursty sequences causing queue tail latencies.
chris: confirmed increased variance in sequence length distribution in the last hour. Batching heuristics probably created long batches.
sre-oncall: immediate mitigations we can apply: 1) lower concurrency per worker 2) enable circuit breaker to cut long-running requests 3) route heavy customers to a fallback model (smaller quantized) 4) enable prefix KV cache where possible.
alex: agree. Proposed short plan: (A) set route concurrency down from 100->40 for api-v2 in us-east-1, (B) push a routing policy to fallback model redwood/gpt-compat-light in same region for customers flagged as high-latency, (C) enable circuit breaker: reject requests >2s queue wait time, (D) temporarily raise autoscaler target by +50% for pool-us-east-1-g4.
maya: will inform customers of mitigation and request sample prompts for repro.
chris: commands I’m going to run on control plane:
```bash
# reduce route concurrency
rictl routes update --name api-v2 --region us-east-1 --concurrency 40
# apply circuit breaker
rictl routes patch --name api-v2 --region us-east-1 --circuit-breaker '{"max_queue_ms":2000,"failure_ratio":0.05}'
# set fallback model for high-lat customers
rictl routing add-fallback --route api-v2 --model redwood/gpt-compat-light --selector "customer.tag:high-throughput"
# scale up dedicated pool quickly
rictl pool scale --name pool-us-east-1-g4 --delta +50
```
olivia: I’ll push the routing change as a canary to 10% of traffic first. If p99 drops at canary we roll to 100%.
chris: also setting temporary token-level rate limit for the flagged customers to 20 rps to reduce tail effects.
maya: support note: asking customers to pause heavy jobs for 30 minutes while we stabilize.
deploy-bot: scheduled change: routing canary -> api-v2 -> 10% @ 1765238200 by chris.
alex: while canary runs, let's capture these metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency (api.v2), GPU queue depth per instance, batch size distribution, kv-cache hit rate, kernel utilization. Datadog queries:
```ddquery
# p99 latency over last 15m
percentile(avg:service.request.latency{service:api-v2,env:prod},99)
# GPU queue depth
avg:gpu.queue_depth{pool:pool-us-east-1-g4} by {instance}
# batch size histogram
avg:requests.batch_size{route:api-v2} by {host}
```
chris: can we also enable a temporary routing rule to prefer us-west region for new requests as a fallback? Less load there.
olivia: yes, but be careful about data residency customers. We'll add a selector to exclude compliance-flagged customers.
sre-oncall: circuit breaker quick config snippet for ops runbook:
```yaml
- route: api-v2
  region: us-east-1
  circuit_breaker:
    max_queue_ms: 2000    # drop if in-queue waiting >2s
    failure_ratio: 0.05  # open if >5% failures in 1m
    cooldown_s: 60
```
alex: tracking repro steps for postmortem: 1) replay sample long prompts from ticket 4287 against hosted api-v2 at high concurrency 2) capture payloads and batch sizes 3) instrument with extra tracing for runtime kernel queue times.
maya: I’ll bundle customer repro artifacts and attach to the support ticket and to the incident doc.
chris: can confirm canary at 10% went out at 1765238200. Early signs: p99 dropped ~30% for canary cohort, but overall cluster p99 still elevated because rest of traffic unchanged.
olivia: rolling to 50% now. Monitoring dashboards: p99 trending down.
alex: good. After 50% rollout, we're seeing overall p95 back to normal and p99 down 55% from peak. We'll keep fallback model in place for 2 hours and continue autoscaler bump for 30 minutes.
sre-oncall: follow-up actions (to add to runbook): - add adaptive batching cap: no batch >512 tokens across requests - add dynamic per-customer concurrency caps - implement automatic fallback when queue latency > threshold - add alert that fires on p99 > baseline*2 for >5m with auto-runbook link.
maya: opened incident ticket INC-2026-184 and added customer comms template.
chris: postmortem TODOs: instrument kernel queue lengths in metrics, tune batching heuristic to avoid mixing short+very long sequences, evaluate if model sharding improves queue fairness.
olivia: we should also add a temporary SLO guardrail: if p99 > 2x baseline, immediately divert 20% of traffic to dedicated fallback pool and reduce route concurrency by 60%. Automate that as a policy.
alex: agreed. I’ll draft the policy and send for review. Thanks everyone — good quick run. :thumbsup: :rotating_light: 
support-bot: customers notified: tickets 4287, 4290, 4292 updated with current mitigation and ETA.
chris: final note: root cause likely batch scheduling + bursty long prompts causing kernel queue congestion. Mitigations applied: concurrency reduced, circuit breaker enabled, fallback model routing, autoscaler bump. Monitoring continues for 30m.
alex: closing thread for now, will link postmortem when drafted. If anything regresses ping @sre-oncall immediately.
